sections.h2: Where is Eagan and what are its boundaries?
sections.html:
Eagan lies in Dakota County south of Saint Paul, with the Minnesota River forming its western edge a short way above the Mississippi confluence. Land area is 31.18 square miles, elevation is about 945 feet, and the 2025 Census estimate is 67,109 people.

The northern edge follows Interstate 494, the eastern edge runs mostly along Minnesota Highway 3, the western edge is the river, and the southern boundary lies about a mile south of Cliff Road. Interstate 35E and Minnesota Highways 13, 55, 77 and 149 are the main routes. The ZIP codes are 55121, 55122 and 55123. The sparsely populated northern part of the city is convenient to the freeways and the Minneapolis-Saint Paul airport, which is why warehouses and distribution centers cluster there.

sections.h2: How did Eagan grow from farmland into a city of 67,000?
sections.html:
The city is named for Patrick Eagan, the first chairman of the town board, who farmed 220 acres near the present town hall. It was settled as an Irish farming community and was once called the onion capital of the United States. The town was established in 1860, and the city incorporated in 1972.

The big jump came in the 1980s, after Highway 77 was relocated and a six-lane bridge was built over the Minnesota River in 1980, followed by the last stretch of Interstate 35E in the mid-1980s.

  • 565 residents in 1860.
  • 3,382 in 1960 and 10,398 in 1970.
  • 20,700 in 1980 and 47,409 in 1990.
  • 63,557 in 2000 and 68,855 in 2020.
  • 67,109 in the 2025 estimate, about 2.5 percent below the 2020 estimate base.

The count more than doubled between 1980 and 1990, so many Eagan houses are now several decades old, and the original roofs, windows and kitchens of that growth period are common in resale listings.

sections.h2: Which employers and school districts matter to Eagan buyers?
sections.html:
Eagan has a large corporate and logistics base. The city's 2025 financial report ranked its largest employers.

  • Thomson Reuters, with 4,500 employees.
  • Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Minnesota, with 3,000.
  • The U.S. Postal Service and Prime Therapeutics, each with about 2,100.
  • UPS with 1,500, Ecolab with 1,400 and the Rosemount-Apple Valley-Eagan school district with 1,075.

The Minnesota Vikings moved their headquarters and practice facility to the former Northwest Airlines site, and the Twin Cities Orthopedics Performance Center opened in 2018. The Census Bureau recorded $1.29 billion in transportation and warehousing receipts in Eagan for 2022.

Schools come from three districts: Rosemount-Apple Valley-Eagan (District 196), West St. Paul-Mendota Heights-Eagan (District 197) and Burnsville-Eagan-Savage (District 191). Eagan High School, Blackhawk Middle School and Dakota Hills Middle School belong to District 196. Confirm the district for an exact address before a listing names a school.

sections.h2: What do ownership and income figures show for Eagan?
sections.html:
A middle-of-the-road Eagan owner-occupied home is valued near $397,000, and about a third of households rent. The table lists the main figures.

sections.h2: Does an Eagan rental license pass to the buyer?
sections.html:
No. Eagan adopted its rental licensing ordinance on March 21, 2023, and licenses are issued each year and are not transferable, so a new owner must apply for a new license.

  • The 2026/27 fee is $165 per year for a single-unit rental, plus a $25 application fee and a $300 conversion fee when an owner-occupied home becomes a rental.
  • Every rental unit is inspected about once every three years or on complaint, and landlords give tenants at least 24 hours of notice.
  • Exempt rentals include units rented to the owner's qualifying relatives, state-licensed housing, rooms inside an owner-occupied home and contract-for-deed purchases recorded with Dakota County.

Late renewal costs 10 percent of the base fee in the first 30 days, 50 percent from 30 to 60 days and 100 percent after 60. Call Community Development at 651-675-5681 before you sell a tenant-occupied house. A buyer who plans to keep tenants has to apply for a license in their own name.

sections.h2: What permit and flood checks come up before an Eagan sale?
sections.html:
Eagan splits permits into two tracks. Building permits go through the online ePermits system, and Building Inspections at 651-675-5675 books inspections in 30-minute slots from 7:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. on weekdays. Zoning permits cover projects that need no building permit, and they are free.

Fences, patios, sport courts, driveway replacements, sidewalks, detached decks below 30 inches, one-story sheds up to 200 square feet, retaining walls under four feet and docks all fall under zoning permits. City staff generally answer within two to five business days. The city's property information page lets you view property records and check for special assessments, and most records include scanned permits, inspection history and site surveys that help a buyer see what was done.

On flood risk, the city says every property is in FEMA Flood Zone X except those in Zone AE along the Minnesota River. The maps date from December 2, 2011, so call the Planning Department or FEMA to confirm an address.

sections.h2: Where does an Eagan deed get recorded?
sections.html:
Dakota County accepts deeds only at its Administration Center in Hastings. Bring them by appointment, or mail them with a cover letter, a return envelope and a phone number to the Property Taxation and Records office at 1590 Highway 55.

The state charges deed tax at 0.33 percent of the net price (Minnesota Statutes 287.21), which on a $397,100 sale comes to about $1,310. Transfer deeds also need a $54 well certificate or a signed well statement. Most county parcels are abstract property, so a title company searches the records before closing. Tax statements and valuation notices appear in the county's Property Information Search, and Property Taxation and Records takes questions at 651-438-4597.

Before you sign, Minnesota Statutes 513.55 has you hand the buyer a written disclosure of the material facts you know.

sections.h2: What are the Dakota County tax dates for an Eagan house?
sections.html:
Dakota County bills real property in halves due May 15 and October 15. The October 2026 date has gone by, and the next deadline is May 15, 2027.

Online payment runs through Paymentus, with a 2.29 percent card fee, a $2.95 Visa debit fee or a $0.35 bank transfer fee, and the phone line is 1-844-797-9075. Walk-in payment is possible at the Hastings, West St. Paul and Apple Valley buildings until 4:30 p.m. on weekdays. A mailed payment needs a postmark on or before the due date. Free automatic payment is open to owners who do not pay through a mortgage company.

Dakota County lists December 31, 2026 as the homestead application deadline, which matters to a buyer who will live in the house. Your closing agent can walk through how the year's tax is prorated.

sections.h2: Which way of selling suits an Eagan house?
sections.html:
An agent listing, a sale by owner and a direct cash purchase are the usual paths. The fit depends on the house, the timeline and whether renters live there.

A listing reaches the broadest set of buyers and suits a house in decent condition with time for showings. A cash purchase can suit a rental owner facing a new license cycle, an owner moving on a short timeline, or a house still carrying decades-old finishes. Ask each buyer for a written price and closing date, pull your permit history and any special assessment record, and weigh what you net, not just the headline figure.

faqs.q: Will the buyer of my Eagan rental house inherit its license?
faqs.a: No. Licenses run for one year and cannot be transferred, so the new owner applies for a fresh rental license. Community Development, at 651-675-5681, can walk through the steps.

faqs.q: Which office takes a deed for recording in Dakota County?
faqs.a: The Property Taxation and Records office in Hastings. Book an appointment, or send the deed by mail to 1590 Highway 55 with a cover letter, return postage and a phone number.

faqs.q: Is my Eagan house in a flood zone?
faqs.a: Almost certainly not. The city says all properties are in FEMA Flood Zone X except those in Zone AE along the Minnesota River. The maps date from 2011, so confirm an address with Planning or FEMA.

faqs.q: Does swapping out a fence or driveway before a sale need city approval in Eagan?
faqs.a: It needs a zoning permit, which is free. Fences, driveway replacements, patios, sheds up to 200 square feet and retaining walls under four feet are covered. Staff usually reply in two to five business days, and the Zoning Hotline is 651-675-5685.

faqs.q: What is the next Dakota County property tax deadline?
faqs.a: May 15, 2027 is the next first-half date, with the second half following on October 15, 2027. The 2026 second half came due on October 15, 2026.
